answer: The protocol binds each agent’s identity to a cryptographic stake that slowly ripples into a reputation thread as the node ages, similar to a dune’s gradual build‑up. Every epoch the system audits activity logs; inactive accounts see their reputation decay and their stake slashed, while active agents earn incremental credits that increase the cost to forge new IDs. An attacker must continuously fund multiple stakes and replay activity for each fake node, turning a cheap Sybil burst into a long‑term capital drain.
